chapter: The 1949 band, breakup and later years
title: Reforming a band in San Diego and growing from eight to eighteen men
summary: With Neal Hefti's charts and Frances Wayne, he started an octet that grew to a big band to honor a Bop City return date.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So after you decided you didn't want to be a manager, then what?

For about the umpteenth time. I started out with a -- I started out with, I think it was about eight men. Let's see. Yeah. And we came down here to San Diego here, and we opened in a place that's no longer there. And Neal Hefti wrote all the charts and Frances Wayne was back singing with me. And we played a bunch of places around. We were here, we spent about six weeks here, and got the thing together, and then we were booked around. We played a whole bunch of one nighters in Arizona and New Mexico, and on up in

the great northwest. In the meantime I had forgotten that I had a return clause engagement with Bop City, and they were insisting on it. And I flipped. I turned -- I was screaming on the telephone and they said, 'Well, you can take your choice. You can bring the little band in or you can come in with the big band, but you're going to come in.' And I thought, well, I can't go in there with a little band, you know, I mean after that other band. So Ray Wetzel was still with me. He was in the trumpet section. And I recollected a lot of guys, Dick Hyfer and some of the other guys, and I started -- now, this is funny. We're booked as an eight piece band, you know, and by the time we got up -- we were up in northern California someplace, I started to collect men for the big band, you know. I kept adding men. And this guy got on the phone to MCA and he said, 'What are you doing? I signed a contract for eight men.' He said, 'Barnet just walked in with 18 men.'

And Hal Howard, was booking it, said, 'Don't worry about it. He's doing something. This isn't going to cost you anything.' But this guy was aghast, you know. He said, 'My God.' I said, 'Don't worry. This is not going to cost you anything,' because I was getting this band together.
